attribution_note: Every row in this file is an OPERATOR'S published statement, quoted with its source and the date this app read it — never asserted as fact and never merged with CDFW's records. Agreement between an operator and CDFW is two rows; disagreement is two rows.
read_at_basis: the OLDEST read date among the operator documents this build actually read. The freshness a reader should be shown is the weakest one contributing to what is on screen, not the newest; link-out-only records are excluded because this app never read them at all.
status_note: Every source below is an operator page this app read on the date the source record names, parsed by a parser written against that page. A parser whose page changes shape raises and fails the build rather than emitting zero rows: zero rows is indistinguishable from 'the operator published nothing', and the app would render a confident, sourced, wrong absence.

sources.source_id: str — stable id, referenced by every plant row
sources.lake_id: str — the operated-lake / directory id this schedule is about
sources.operator: str — the operator's legal name, as the operator writes it
sources.document_title: str|null — the operator's own heading, verbatim
sources.kind: scheduled | reported | next_plant_undated | quote_only | not_machine_readable | link_only — WHAT THE OPERATOR PUBLISHES, which is what decides whether a row can exist at all. The last three carry zero rows by definition: prose this app quotes rather than parses, a schedule published as an image, and a schedule this app will never read because the operator's own site says not to.
sources.machine_readable: bool — false means quote and link out, never OCR
sources.forward_schedule: bool — true only for a document that lists dates AHEAD. A forward schedule may never emit an `occurred` row: a schedule saying a date is not a source saying the stock happened.
sources.never_fetched: bool — true only on a `link_only` source. This app has never read the page and will not; `read_at` on such a record is the date the LINK-OUT POLICY was recorded, and a renderer must not print it as a read date.
sources.policy_reason: str|null — MANDATORY when never_fetched; why this app does not read it
sources.covers_start: date|null — the first date the DOCUMENT ITSELF printed
sources.covers_end: date|null — the last date the DOCUMENT ITSELF printed, not this app's week anchoring of it; EXPIRY IS DERIVED ON DEVICE FROM THIS
sources.status_at_build: current | expired — PROVENANCE ONLY. Never drives a UI state: a boolean stored in a dataset that is static between OTA pulls is only ever true relative to the build that wrote it.
sources.operator_stamp: printed | page_modified | null — WHICH KIND of date this is
sources.operator_stamp_text: str|null — e.g. the words printed on an image
sources.caveats: [str] — the operator's own caveat sentences, verbatim, interned here
sources.closure_note: str|null — MANDATORY when the caveats contain a closure statement. It renders as its own attributed line on every scheduled row, without a tap: 'stocked lakes are closed on stock days' is the most actionable sentence an operator publishes and the one a driver most needs.
sources.heading_text: str|null — the operator's own section heading, for a quote_only source
sources.quotes: [{heading, text}] — for a quote_only source: every stock-mentioning paragraph, verbatim, under the operator's own sub-heading. Every one of them, not a chosen one; picking one is editing.
sources.assets: [{url, alt, upload_path_month}] — for an image schedule: the images themselves, so the app can link to what it cannot read. `upload_path_month` is the CMS upload month in the image URL, which is an asset upload date and NOT an edit date.
sources.transcription: {by, on, asset_url, asset_sha256}|null — when machine_readable is false

plants.source_id: str — joins to sources[].source_id; caveats are never repeated per row
plants.kind: scheduled | occurred | delayed | cancelled | unscheduled. `occurred` ONLY where the source's own text is retrospective; a now-past date on a forward schedule stays `scheduled`, because a schedule saying a date is not a source saying the stock happened.
plants.week_of: date|null — the Sunday-anchored cell this row lands in, so every source lands in one cell. NULL, and only null, for a `month`- or `none`-precision row: the operator named no week, and one hedged sentence must not paint a mark on the four or five cells a month touches. Those rows render once, as a note, above the strip.
plants.week_end: date|null — the Saturday of `week_of`; null wherever week_of is
plants.date: date|null — present ONLY when the source stated a day
plants.date_precision: day | week | month | none — never widened, never narrowed
plants.quantity_text: str|null — the operator's own string, never re-unitised and never summed. Null where the row printed more than one quantity: choosing between '4000 DFW Plant … + 2000 Pound Private Plant' is arithmetic.
plants.detail: str|null
plants.verbatim: str — MANDATORY; what a tap shows
plants.date_text: str|null — the exact substring of `verbatim` the date was parsed from. The build fails when it is not inside `verbatim`, which is what makes the parse checkable against the operator's own words.
plants.attribution: str — '<Operator> states'

caveats: We stock trout throughout the year, weather permitting. Typically last stock is May/June - depending on water temperature and conditions.
Additional stocks possible of catfish or panfish when available/in season.
sources.cadence_statement: We stock trout throughout the year, weather permitting. Typically last stock is May/June - depending on water temperature and conditions.
We typically start planting in late October and continue through the first part of May as long as conditions permit.

quotes.heading: Trout
quotes.text: Our last trout stock was on April 16, 2026. Any remaining fish have not been seen for a while. There may be some still in the water, but they will likely remain elusive especially with the warmer days we are experiencing. Look out for our Trout Stock Schedule releasing soon for the 26-27 season!

quotes.heading: Catfish
quotes.text: Catfish have been caught from the fishing float, shallows, and off of boats in deep water. September 28th was our last stock for the season, but there are still plenty of fish in the water. There has not been much of a reliable bite during the heat of the day, but the mornings and evenings have been productive. Try using some chopped mackerel, shrimp, chicken livers, dough baits, and even Power Bait.

sources.page_modified_basis: WordPress upload path in the schedule image URL (…/uploads/YYYY/MM/…) — an asset upload month, not an edit date and not a read date
sources.cadence_statement: Lake Jennings is stocked with trout weekly or bi-weekly between November and early April, and with channel catfish during the summer months.

sources.policy_reason: ebparks.org is classified `restricted` and is additionally in `NEVER_FETCH_HOSTS`, so no code path in this pipeline can reach it. Three separate signals, any one of which would be enough: its Cloudflare robots.txt names ClaudeBot, GPTBot and CCBot among nine blocked agents; it publishes `Content-Signal: ai-train=no,use=reference`; and its terms of use forbid using its materials "on any other website or networked computer environment". The District does publish stocking dates for these six lakes. This app does not read them, and will not — it names the operator, says the schedule is on the operator's own site, and offers the link.

licence_statements.note: Two statements by the same operator, on the same site, in tension. This app quotes both with their own pages and read dates and picks neither — the same rule it applies to a CDFW/operator disagreement about a plant.

statements.quote: No State fishing license required; a fishing permit from the General Store, Gatehouse or our Santee Lakes’ App is all you need!
The District may require anglers over the age of sixteen to obtain a valid California State Fishing License issued by the California Department of Fish and Game.
